title: Federal Reserve, Clearing and Treasury
question: Who may access, clear, settle or control public money and collateral across the Federal Reserve, Treasury and private clearing utilities?
bluf: The September 29 Federal Reserve OIG evaluation closes the criminal and administrative-misconduct allegations within its scope but finds a serious management failure: the Board did not effectively execute the Eccles-1951 construction-manager-at-risk contract, had no agreed project-level guaranteed maximum price after more than $2,000,000,000 was awarded, underused its owner representative, allowed 84 limited-scope packages to set price without an overall ceiling and repeatedly reported the project as on track against rebased benchmarks. Construction rose from a $921,000,000 February 2020 budget to a $2,018,000,000 December 2024 budget; four MEP awards alone rose from a $206,000,000 estimate to $694,000,000. Inflation and site/design conditions mattered, but the OIG found the criticized marble, fountains, garden terrace and related features were not material cost drivers. Chairman Warsh concurred and directed GSA project leadership, an independent cost audit, GMP negotiations, fixed metrics and contract remedies; these are directed corrective actions, not yet a ceiling, validated final cost or recovered dollar. The September 29 American Express feedback dispute exposes a resolution-planning classification seam: the Federal Reserve and FDIC identified significant uncertainty in the feasibility of a one-buyer sale across an FDIC bank receivership and two Chapter 11 estates, yet found no deficiency or shortcoming. Regulation QQ permits additional feedback, but its shortcoming definition uses closely related feasibility language; Gould's dissent therefore targets the opacity and structural leverage of unclassified feedback, not the statutory existence of living wills. The September 20 legal-status and records-routing matrix establishes that the Federal Reserve has no single public/private status: the answer varies by actor, function, statute, record custody and remedy. The Board is a federal agency; the FOMC is an APA/FOIA agency; each Reserve Bank is a separate federally chartered corporation whose agency, instrumentality, employer, person and liability status changes by legal regime. Records likewise route by function and control rather than physical host: Bank-held material can be an FOMC record, a current-rule Board record, or a Bank record subject to the Banks' voluntary transparency policy and other lawful access routes. The companion appointment, removal and succession chain maps five distinct personnel constitutions from Governors and Reserve Bank directors through FOMC officers, SOMA management, the Inspector General and Bank general auditors; it also restores the August whole-government FRFS/National IT committee constitution to the direct package's discovery routes. The Wave 4 reconciliation confirms that the prior committee map was already substantial and classifies its bodies by legal effect: statutory Board/FOMC/Bank-board decisions, Board advisory and delegated routes, PSPAC policy advice, COP/Payments Committee/AFRC/ITOC enterprise governance, CPE/FRFS management, Richmond/National IT hosting and independent assurance. It distinguishes PCSC, PSPAC and the presidents' Payments Committee and preserves the unpublished charters, votes, materiality tests and application RACI as proof gaps. Wave 5 separates inspection and recommendation from approval, conditioning, direction, injunction, removal and institutional suspension. It finds extensive but nonuniversal audit, preserves GAO's monetary-policy exclusions and Dodd-Frank exceptions, defines the clean 2025 outside-audit limits, and locates actual stopping power in Board/Bank-board/FOMC/Treasury/court/congressional instruments rather than in the audit label itself. Wave 6 finds no unitary Federal Reserve crisis commander: insured-bank resolution, daylight and Discount Window credit, §13(3), FOMC/SOMA operations, payment and cyber incidents, Buddy Reserve Bank continuity, §248(h) intervention, cash logistics and Treasury fiscal-agent recovery have distinct legal principals, operators, books, finality and exit rules. It separates participant buddy banks from inter-Reserve-Bank continuity and service restoration from transaction reconciliation. Wave 7 reconstructs the twelve corporations' foundation: the Federal Reserve Act is the congressional charter; filing a district organization certificate created the body corporate; the Comptroller's separate certificate authorized business; and bylaws govern internally beneath federal law. It inventories all twelve current-posted bylaws and twenty-four Branches, distinguishes statutory member stock from ordinary equity, and identifies the direct St. Louis certificate plus exact missing constitutive, election, seal and title records. The September 20 congressional-oversight map shows why the Federal Reserve is not legally a fourth constitutional branch while preserving the real accountability critique: Congress created the System, controls its statutes and institutional design, confirms Governors through the Senate, mandates testimony, reports, audits and disclosures, and can amend or repeal the architecture; yet self-funding, long protected terms, nonconfirmed Reserve Bank presidents, GAO exclusions, OIG jurisdictional seams and monetary-policy exceptions deliberately insulate immediate policy operations. The vault-canonical factual spine and current Workbench extensions show how the Fed can retain the dollar unit and crisis backstop while private clearing moves into the middle and the twelve Reserve Banks specialize inside a common operating machine. The whole-site evidence supports contested functional unbundling and reduced daily visibility, not established castration, abolition, merger, private capture or removal. The September 20 dollar-issuance constitution shows that the Federal Reserve's role is a congressional statutory operating arrangement, not a private agreement or transfer of U.S. sovereignty. Congress defines the unit and legal-tender system; Treasury issues coins, retains capped United States-note authority and prints Federal Reserve notes; the Board orders and authorizes those notes; Reserve Banks issue notes into circulation and maintain central-bank balances; and private deposits and stablecoins remain legally distinct claims. Congress can restructure or replace that architecture by ordinary federal law, while executive orders, regulations and operator contracts cannot rewrite the statute. The companion congressional change history proves this is not merely theoretical: from 1927 corporate succession and the 1930s governance and gold rewrites through the 1977 objectives, 1980 monetary-and-payment reach, 2008 interest on reserves, 2010 emergency-credit limits and 2025–26 digital-money boundaries, Congress has repeatedly expanded, constrained and reallocated Fed powers. It also separates legislative dissolution from violation-based franchise forfeiture and the public dollar unit from Federal Reserve notes and private redeemable dollar claims. The Oklahoma City hearing audit shows that Congress was hardening the digital-public-money boundary, but the June 12 exchange did not establish illegal CBDC issuance or a §11(h) forfeiture case: no current Fed policymaker admitted ongoing work, the enacted §16A prohibition postdated the hearing, the House text predated it, and the public post-order projects reviewed do not establish creation of a U.S. central-bank liability. The September 20 payment-system mandate map shows that fostering safety and efficiency is a major Federal Reserve function but not a unitary third mandate parallel to Federal Reserve Act §2A. Congress supplied tool-specific powers that the Board, twelve Reserve Banks, private operators and co-regulators exercise through operation, access, intraday liquidity, rules, supervision, oversight and coordination; safety, efficiency and accessibility must therefore be tested at each lifecycle layer. The September 16 interest-rate constitution adds the missing rate-setting process: the FOMC target, administered tools, transaction benchmarks, auctions, traded yields and customer contracts are separate objects, and private, tax, insider, public-credit and credit-union below-market lanes have different authority and consequence. Its overnight-money companion follows the actual reserve-account, Fedwire, unsecured-credit, rollover and ON RRP mechanics beneath the policy rate and distinguishes Federal Reserve balances from commercial nostro/vostro claims. The September 18 DTCC whole-site refresh supports a regulated modular-conversion reading: DTCC is rebuilding legal submission, machine-readable reporting, operating hours, fund distribution, asset records and settlement interfaces while preserving incumbent membership, account, risk, correction and finality controls. AnnounceDirect, CMU CSV conversion, Fund/SERV tokenization access, 24x5 clearing, DTC tokenization and settlement modernization remain distinct objects with distinct proof gates rather than one common launch.
evidence_cutoff_note: The September 20 congressional-oversight addition is a U.S. primary-source orientation through 21:00 EDT. It separates Congress's ultimate statutory control from operational command; incorporates Federal Reserve Act appointment, funding, reporting and audit provisions, 31 U.S.C. §714, 5 U.S.C. §807, official committee jurisdiction, OIG limits and the 2025–26 Supreme Court independence decisions; and does not treat a hearing, report, nomination or audit as equivalent to enacted law or an FOMC direction. The September 20 dollar-issuance addition is a foundational U.S. constitutional and primary-statutory orientation through 19:00 EDT. It incorporates the July 2026 Federal Reserve Act §16A retail-CBDC prohibition, preserves the distinct GENIUS Act private-stablecoin lane, and maps ordinary-legislation, administrative and constitutional-amendment change paths without treating a proposal or executive order as self-executing currency authority. The September 20 Oklahoma City hearing audit is current through 18:49 EDT. It uses the official House event and legislative record plus a locally preserved automatic-caption transcript; no formal hearing transcript, Davidson exhibit, post-order San Francisco CBDC job posting or authoritative Executive Order 14178 violation finding was located. The September 20 payment-system mandate addition is a foundational U.S. primary-source orientation through 18:00 EDT. It distinguishes the institutional function from the Federal Reserve Act §2A mandate and maps legal authority, Board/Reserve-Bank/private/co-regulator roles, safety, efficiency, access, lifecycle and measurement without claiming plenary Board jurisdiction. The separate September 20 addition resolves the public outcome of the seven-request discount-rate sequence—all twelve district tables show 4.00% effective September 17—while preserving the remaining-five timing question for the later minutes, and records the SVB review's new monthly exam-team escalation path to supervision leadership and the respective Reserve Banks. The September 18 addition is a whole-site DTCC refresh and does not turn the approximate October tokenization target into an exact launch. Prior studies retain their own cutoffs.
use_note: For Shelton, separate appointment, advisory access, proposal, legal authority, debt-management adoption, gold control, auction, settlement and redemption; do not collapse a limited gold-linked bond into a classical gold standard, universal dollar convertibility, gold revaluation or a live stablecoin-reserve program. Internal recall for dated institutional actions and actor/clock distinctions. Follow each claim to primary sources; the bridge essay is interpretive and must be read against its companion factual refresh. Functional castration does not establish abolition, a Reserve Bank merger or a Board takeover. Exclude local-STT quotation, undisclosed counterparties and pending pension/payment-stack interpretations. For conference records, keep event, prepared text, spoken record, searchable transcript and later institutional consequence separate.

availability_semantics.public_reading: The public site contains both the original public view and a crawler-friendly static HTML reading edition. public_full_text is true.
availability_semantics.public_machine_data: The public site contains the complete positively selected structured dataset. public_full_text is true; reading_url and data_url identify the canonical JSON object.
availability_semantics.private_library_metadata: The governed private Research Library contains the material, but the public site exposes only safe title, role and state metadata. public_full_text is false and access_state is private_by_design. Do not infer its contents.

retrieval_instructions: Open full_text_url for the package before treating a summary as the underlying research.
For a public reading, prefer reading_url. For public_machine_data, open data_url and preserve its schema_version, data_as_of, scope_boundary and evidence vocabulary.
A failure to retrieve public_full_text is an access or crawler problem, not a private-by-design signal.
For access_state private_by_design, use metadata only and do not infer contents.
Preserve the package evidence cutoff, evidence_cutoff_note and any material-specific as_of date. Verify time-sensitive claims with fresh primary sources.
Keep fact, project inference, strongest rival, unresolved object and falsifier separate.
